ui_bugs.issue: data-testid uses 0-based array index (setting-reflvl-0-name .. setting-reflvl-4-name), but on-screen rows are labelled #1..#5 and the task acceptance spec expected setting-reflvl-1..5. Functionality works; only the testid numbering is inconsistent with the visible level number.

design_issues.screen: Rewards page hero (user at exactly threshold)
issues: When count equals the previous tier's min_referrals exactly (e.g. 5 refs while sitting on Ignite), progress bar to next tier shows 0% even though the text says '5 / 10'. Formula `done = count - prev_min` yields 0 at the entry of a tier — visually confusing. Consider showing done = count - prev_min still but using span between current tier min and next tier min: 5/10 fills the bar at 50% based on absolute count.

The atomic claim uses $addToSet + $inc on claimed_referral_levels — this correctly prevents double-claim under race. Good.
GET /api/referrals/rewards returns raw ints/floats without a Pydantic response model — okay for MVP but consider defining a ReferralRewardsOut model for consistency.
Rewards.jsx progress calculation on the client mirrors backend (uses next_level_needs); OK. But hero shows '5 more to unlock ₦1,500' — string composition looks correct.

AdminSettings referral-level array uses map index as key AND as testid; if admin removes a middle level, remaining testids re-index, which will confuse automated tests. Prefer stable keys tied to lvl.level.
